title: Retrospective Ingest Safeguard with Traffic Shaping and Idempotent Delta Apply
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a conservative, operator-friendly backfill/replay tool that applies retrospective telemetry deltas into the usage analytics warehouse without violating SLOs or producing duplicate metrics. Core features: (1) idempotent delta computation at event-key granularity, (2) request-rate shaping against ingestion endpoints and analytics pipelines, (3) resume tokens and safe checkpoints to allow incremental backfill restarts, (4) preflight dry-run mode that computes projected volume/latency/cost, and (5) an operator UI in Console to visualize backfill progress and cancel/trim windows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Backfill job can compute and apply deltas idempotently for a 30-day window with no duplicated aggregates when run twice. 2) Traffic shaping limits ensure average pipeline input does not exceed configured headroom and will throttle at 95pct configured target. 3) Resume tokens persist to durable storage and allow restart within 1 minute of previous checkpoint. 4) Dry-run provides a projected token/ingestion cost estimate within 10% of actual run. 5) Console shows progress and a per-route risk score for operators.
approach_notes: We will implement a separate 'retro-ingest' worker that reads canonical telemetry from the raw event lake, computes deterministic deltas using a stable event fingerprint (customer_id + route_id + event_ts + schema_hash), and writes patch records to a write-ahead store before applying to the warehouse. The worker will use the existing replayer orchestration for windowed runs but introduce a traffic-shaping token bucket per-target (ingest-api, warehouse-loader) with dynamic headroom derived from current SLO buffers. Retention of resume tokens to S3 and integration with job-status in Console will be added.
tradeoffs:
- Strong idempotency requires more memory for de-duplication caches or additional round-trip lookups to the write-ahead store, increasing cost.
- Aggressive traffic shaping keeps production safe but extends backfill time; we'll provide an operator knob to prioritize speed vs safety.
- Adding a write-ahead patch store simplifies rollback but adds a new operational component to monitor.
risks: 1) Underestimated rate of historical events may cause prolonged backfill beyond SLA windows. 2) Non-deterministic third-party schema changes can create false deltas. 3) Resume-token corruption could leave partial state applied; mitigation is to verify checksums on resume and provide manual reconciliation tools.
test_plan: Unit tests for delta computation and fingerprint stability, integration tests that run the worker against a synthetic event lake with injected duplicates/late-arrivals, chaos test that simulates pipeline throttling and restarts to validate resume tokens, and an internal canary run on a low-volume customer window before tenant-wide rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag. 2) Run dry-run on 7-day window for internal telemetry account and compare projected vs actual. 3) Canary backfill a single low-risk customer (<1% global traffic) for a 30-day window with traffic shaping set to 30% headroom. 4) Ramp to 10% then 50% with operator sign-offs. 5) Full roll when metrics stable and no regression for two consecutive days.
metrics: Backfill duration, applied_delta_count, duplicate_rate (should be 0), ingestion_throttle_events, average_pipeline_latency, projected_vs_actual_cost_delta
